q-21051.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14227715/assets/c85e6ee974a59d956367634fdd1d57b65e9d42a980fe1750886527b173f05d32.png)

Find $BM$ given that the area of $△ACB$ is $49\,{cm}^{2},$ $AM=5\,cm,$ and $MC=9\,cm.$

(Figure not drawn to scale)
q-21051.worked_solution:
The area of the triangle is defined as 

$$
A=\frac{b\cdot h}{2},
$$

 where $b$ is the base and $h$ is the corresponding height.

From the diagram, we see that the height is $h=BM,$ and the corresponding base is 

$$
b=AM+MC=14\,cm.
$$

Therefore, using the formula for the area, we can solve for the height as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{b\cdot h}{2} \\ 49 & =\frac{14\cdot h}{2} \\ 98 & =14\cdot h \\ h & =\frac{98}{14} \\ h & =7\,cm\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, $BM=7\,\text{cm}.$

q-87851.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14227715/assets/678c719915b0d27c1378548267123cfbac3f13f13ee0a05fd6dacd85164911f6.png)

What is the area of the right triangle $ABC$ shown above?
q-87851.worked_solution:
Since $m∠A=m∠C={45}^{∘}$ and $AB=BC,$ we have an isosceles right triangle. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14227715/assets/4d340b37161cb3f970ba588fa15a21b3a35ee376c5766e92d6c48358d4ed003e.png)

Therefore, the area of the triangle is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}AB\cdot BC \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot {5}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 25 \\  & =12.5\,.\end{aligned}
$$
